1.0.7.3 addresses the loudest bug reports from GitHub issues and the r/jellyfin + r/JellyfinCommunity threads.

Recycle bin: overhauled with rich per-row metadata (BinPath, Provenance, Reason, IssueType, ActionText, RestoreHint, auto-purge countdown), origin-manifest sidecars so restores survive history loss, cross-volume consolidation of legacy bin locations, non-destructive restore that suffixes -restored instead of overwriting, and a 3 GB / 5 GB free-space floor that pauses fix runs and refuses config save on a full bin volume. New endpoints: /RecycleBin/OtherBins, /RecycleBin/Consolidate, /RecycleBin/DiskInfo.

Duplicate detection: keys now include ProductionYear so remakes stop collapsing (#3), keeper picker excludes symlinks and 0-byte files (F-098), DuplicateMinAgeDays default 7 to 0 with one INFO line naming vetoed count.

Fixer output: TrackFixer + TranscodeFixer restore source CreationTimeUtc and LastWriteTimeUtc so Recently-Added stays honest (#31); dry-run stale-failure path no longer flips vanished files to Fixed; per-sidecar history fan-out via FixResult.AdditionalRecycled gives every recycled sidecar its own Restore button; subtitle-provider quota mid-run is now detected and handled quietly.

Playability: cross-checks ffprobe format_name against extension so an MKV renamed .mp3 emits container-extension-mismatch (F-213). HasTruncationMarker no longer treats the benign Truncating packet warning as truncation - that warning fires on real-world MKV cluster boundaries, MPEG-TS packet alignment, and MP4 mdat overlap on files that play fine in Jellyfin (Reddit reports: friskyapple, oogoom, moonplaza, Commercial-Camp-8052). Only File ended prematurely now counts.

TrackFixer ffmpeg command gains -fflags +genpts at input and -avoid_negative_ts make_zero at output - fixes the mpegts sample rate not set / Could not write header failure on Blu-ray-derived .m2ts sources, and lets OutputVerifier accept legitimate long-form duration drift (#39, slack widened from fixed 2 s to max(2 s, dur x 2 percent)).

Combined ffmpeg pass (#28, #32): FixTask now detects same-file AudioLanguage + SubtitleLanguage pairs before the fix loop and routes them through a new TrackFixer.FixCombinedAsync so one ffmpeg drops both categories in a single pass instead of two back-to-back remuxes. Two history rows recorded, one bin entry, both issues flip to Fixed.

SMART noise dedup: SmartHealthProbeWmi caches per-drive-letter WMI failures and SmartHealthProbe caches per-device smartctl timeout / IO / non-zero-exit failures. First failure per device per session still emits the diagnostic; subsequent failures on the same device are suppressed until restart. Addresses the Errors-tab spam on NVMe + mount-point setups (#38, #23).

Files: new read-only Jellyfin logs shortcut at the file-browser root supporting listing + per-file download so users can attach logs to bug reports; ApiKey= param renamed from api_key= for Jellyfin 10.10+ compatibility.

Diagnostics: Copy diagnostics button relabelled Report an issue (copies diagnostics + opens issue tracker in a new tab).

Reliability hotfix: fixes the "13 files locked, nothing holding them" report class by switching every scanner/probe (ArtworkScanner, NfoScanner, TrickplayOptimizeScanner, BookProbeService, FileHasher) from File.OpenRead (default FileShare.Read blocks concurrent moves/deletes on Windows and shows up as ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION 32) to a new MediaFileHelper.OpenSharedRead helper using FileShare.ReadWrite | Delete. Also splits FixTask's catch-all "disk error" into four accurate diagnostic keys — FixTask.FileMissing (marks issue Fixed so retry stops), FixTask.FileLocked (sharing violation post-retry), FixTask.DiskFull (real ENOSPC only, HResult 112/39/28), residual FixTask.IOError; every bucket gets a new Errors-tab entry with actionable copy. Adds a 5s per-library-root probe to ScanTask so a hard-mounted dead NFS/SMB share can't hang the ThreadPool and force LXC restarts — unreachable roots are skipped with a diagnostic pointing at soft,timeo=30,retrans=3 mount flags. Cleans up Ffmpeg.Timeout noise on Blu-ray remuxes: TrackFixer's 30-min first pass no longer surfaces to Errors (only the 5-hour retry's failure does), Track.RemuxRetry diagnostic removed as it fired on the happy path. New README Uninstall section explaining the remove-repo -> uninstall -> restart sequence so Jellyfin's Update Plugins task can't race the deleteOnStartup marker. Still one binary for both Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0.

Duplicate detection rework with a per-pair confidence ladder (Exact 1.00 / Identified 0.90 / Heuristic 0.70) plus two hard vetoes (title-token Jaccard, runtime delta) that kill the GitHub #3 Futurama-specials false-positive class.

Fixes
- GitHub #3 - duplicate false positives on distinct files sharing an episode metadata slot.
- GitHub #12 - container CPU/RAM cards showed HOST numbers; now read cgroup v2 -> v1 first and fall through to /proc only when unbounded.
- GitHub #6 + #12-SMART - Linux SMART reported Unknown forever on drives whose libraries live on a partition; now walks partition -> disk via lsblk.
- ArtworkFixer clears the item's ImageInfos BEFORE deleting the file on disk so /Items/{id}/Images/Primary stops 404-ing after a corrupt-artwork sweep.
- Dry-run is now airtight: MissingSubtitleFixer no longer queries external subtitle providers under dry-run (was leaking which files exist and burning provider quota).
- Field report A1: default-threaded ffmpeg pinned every core on a 1-2 vCPU Docker VM and locked up SSH. Threads default to max(1, ProcessorCount/2).
- Field reports A9/A10: reworded 'original kept in recycle bin' and dry-run preview action text so users stop reading it as 'MediaDash is hoarding files'.
- Field report B1: sidecars now follow the primary file after a successful move.
- Field report B4: subtitles in Subtitles/ or Subs/ subfolders next to media are detected.
- Field report D2: MissingSubtitle now runs before Transcode so subtitles land before an encode that would rename-orphan them.
- NfoScanner no longer flags valid metadata as corrupt on missing per-Actor extensions or trailing text after </movie>.
- OrphanCleanupScanner: unrelated adjacent folders no longer treated as orphans; scanners emitting non-video paths opt out of scoped-delete so stale rows don't sit forever.
- EmbeddedCoverArtScanner: no longer flags every non-trivial AVI as corrupt.
- SmartHealth probe: no longer stuck on 'Checking SMART status...' forever on probe crash; PowerShell reliability-counter fallback no longer silently misses on trailing whitespace in FriendlyName.
- RecycleBin cross-volume move: .mediadash.tmp staging file is cleaned up when a move throws mid-way.
- LibraryMonitor: ReportFileSystemChanged now fires for both source and destination on move so cached ImageInfo drops.

Privacy
- Anonymous community-stats install ID is now month-rotated: SHA-256(salt || Jellyfin SystemId || year-month), never stored on disk. Prior persistent UUID was stronger linkability than APP/GDPR tolerates for 'aggregate community stats'.

Duplicates - new config
- DuplicateAutoFixConfidence (default 0.80): under Automatic mode, only pairs at or above this confidence are auto-queued.
- DuplicateTitleJaccardVeto (default 0.40): kills pairs whose filename title tokens overlap less than this.
- DuplicateRuntimeVetoPct (default 15%): kills pairs whose runtimes differ by more than this.
- New file_hashes cache table and Confidence column on issues (idempotent migration to schema v4).

Still one binary for both Jellyfin 10.11 and 12.0.

Full-scanner community stats, on-by-default opt-in, and first-run wizard layout polish. Dashboard's fix-completion popup and redownload banner now survive a plugin reload.

Features
- Community stats now cover every scanner MediaDash ships. 8 new scanners added to the payload, backend schema, and public views (Ungrouped, LargeTrickplay, SubtitleFonts, OrphanedDebris, CorruptNfo, HeavyTranscode, FailedTranscode, EmbeddedCoverArt) alongside the existing 10.
- Community stats default flipped from off to on for new installs. Existing installs are unchanged; their persisted AnalyticsEnabled value wins. The first-run wizard shows the checkbox pre-ticked; untick in Settings -> Safety at any time to opt out.
- Dashboard's LastFixRun (fix-completion popup) and RedownloadWarnings (Overview banner) are now persisted to the plugin DB via a write-through wrapper. Previously both dropped on every plugin reload, so a mid-day restart made the popup or banner vanish. Rehydrated on plugin start.
- README's community-impact table, docs/index.html impact section, and the monthly-stats GitHub Actions workflow now render rows for all 18 scanner types. docs/PRIVACY.md field table extended to match; opt-out language rewritten throughout.
- Docs screenshots (overview, issues, history, settings) regenerated against the current UI with Blender open-movie sample data - no personal filenames or hostnames.

Bug fixes
- First-run wizard "Skip walkthrough" now mints the anonymous install UUID when analytics is enabled. Previously, skipping the wizard left the ID empty and the reporter silently no-op'd, so an on-by-default install that never completed the walkthrough never actually contributed a single row.

Reclaim totals now match across the plugin, heavy-transcode fixer works on well-encoded sources, SMART shows correctly on unprivileged Linux, and the History tab lets you slice failures by reason.

Features
- History tab's Failed filter now surfaces a "search by reason" dropdown listing the distinct failure reasons in your history with a count each (Permission denied, I/O error, Cross-device link, File no longer exists, etc.). Selecting one narrows the list; switching the top-level chip clears it.
- SMART pill on the Overview drives now shows a specific hint when smartctl fails due to permissions on Linux: setcap 'cap_sys_rawio+ep' $(which smartctl) for native installs, --cap-add=SYS_RAWIO --device=... for Docker.

Bug fixes
- Overview "Reclaimed since install" and History tab's summary + per-library chart now show the same number. History was summing the paginated 500-row window client-side while Overview summed the entire history server-side, causing the mismatch (e.g. 599 GB vs 8.1 GB). New /History/Stats endpoint aggregates over all history server-side; both panels source the total from it.
- Heavy-transcode / failed-transcode fixes no longer refuse to swap when the re-encoded file is slightly larger than the original. Those fix types exist for direct-play compatibility, not disk savings â€” the size gate is now Quality-only, with a 30% hard cap on the transcode types to guard against misconfigured encode settings.
- SMART pills now appear on library drives on Linux. Library-drive detection was using Path.GetPathRoot which always returns "/" on Linux â€” no library drive was ever flagged, so the SMART probe never ran there. Now uses the deepest-matching mount point via FindDriveForPath.
- smartctl exit_status is now honoured. Non-zero exit (permission denied, unsupported device, no SMART support) returns Unknown with the actual smartctl error message, instead of being mis-interpreted as "self-assessment FAILED".

New Overview banner warns when a MediaDash re-encode gets undone by something external (typically Sonarr/Radarr redownloading a "too-small" file whose size dropped below the quality profile minimum, but also fires on manual recycle-bin restores or backup-restore overwrites).

Detection is evidence-based, not guessed: at the end of every scan MediaDash walks the last 30 days of successful non-dry-run history entries, and for each one where the ORIGINAL is still preserved in the recycle bin, compares the file currently at the same path against the recycled original. If the current file is within 10% of the original size â€” i.e. the same rough size we shrank down â€” the shrunk copy has been replaced. Only paths meeting that concrete size-match trigger the warning. False positives are limited to genuine restores, which are also worth surfacing.

The red banner shows the filename, the shrunk-to size, the current size, and the fix date. Dismissable per browser session; reappears on the next scan if the condition still holds.

Two fixes and a reclaim.

VAAPI hardware encodes now pass -rc_mode VBR to hevc_vaapi / h264_vaapi / av1_vaapi. Mesa VAAPI's default rate-control is CQP, which ignores -b:v/-maxrate and picks a QP that routinely produces output LARGER than a modest-bitrate source â€” the "the re-encoded file would be larger than the original, so the original was kept" retry loop that some AMD iGPU users saw every 30-70 minutes on the same file. VBR honours -b:v as the target and -maxrate as the ceiling, so the encoder actually stays under the requested bitrate.

Orphan sidecar sweep: at the end of every fix run (right after the recycle bin purge), MediaDash now walks each library root and deletes any *.mediadash.tmp*, *.mediadash.new*, mediadash.tmp.*, or mediadash.new.* file it finds. These are leftovers from a hard-killed encode (SIGKILL, container restart, Jellyfin crash) where the C# finally block that normally deletes them never ran. Deleted-count + reclaimed-bytes go into Jellyfin's log.

FfmpegExecutor now sweeps for orphaned MediaDash ffmpeg processes before spawning a new encode. Linux only (reads /proc/<pid>/cmdline; Windows/macOS would need extra deps for a very rare failure mode). Any ffmpeg whose command line contains a mediadash.tmp or mediadash.new marker is killed with SIGKILL and its sidecar output file is deleted. Prevents the "two ffmpegs writing to the same output" scenario after a plugin hot-reload or a Jellyfin restart mid-encode. Also cleans up the interleaved-bytes .tmp file that would otherwise sit on disk until the next fix run on the same source overwrote it.

name: Marquee Companion [✓]
description:
Adds server-side library filtering by media-stream characteristics that Jellyfin's core API can't express (video dynamic range, codecs, audio channel count, and spatial audio), opt-in recovery of missing release dates from file names or date added, authenticated Apple Watch media grants, and server-stored profile PINs. The filtering API exposes a paginated, BaseItemDto-compatible endpoint and a capability endpoint for client feature-detection. Release-date recovery is selected per library and can preview changes before applying them.

versions.changelog:
- Initial release. - Resolution (isHd/is4K) passthrough for client filtering. - Fix: filtering by a library returned no items. The library (parentId) is now
  resolved into its contents so video range / codec / audio filters work when
  scoped to a specific library.
- Renamed the plugin to "Marquee Companion" (display name only; API route,
  plugin id, and behavior unchanged).
- Capabilities are now scoped to the requested library (parentId): the available
  values offered for a library are drawn only from items in that library, so any
  single facet selection is guaranteed to match at least one item there. Omitting
  parentId still returns the global value set.
- TV libraries now filter correctly by stream facets. Stream attributes live on
  episodes, but TV libraries are browsed at the series level; the filter now
  matches episodes and returns the shows that have at least one matching episode.
  Also forces a recursive query so a library id resolves to its contents.
- Added opt-in recent podcast discovery through Podcast Index. - Podcast discovery now logs why it returned nothing. The endpoint still answers 404 for
  every failure, but the server log distinguishes disabled credentials, a Podcast Index
  rejection, and feeds dropped during validation — including a per-rule tally of what was
  dropped.
- Removes the YouTube trailer resolver. Clients now hand YouTube trailers to the YouTube
  app instead, so the server no longer downloads, verifies, updates, or executes yt-dlp or a
  JavaScript runtime.
- Removes the yt-dlp and JavaScript-runtime downloads earlier versions installed. Those
  binaries are unreachable now the resolver is gone, so the plugin reclaims the directory it
  created rather than leaving an administrator to find it. Only its own install root is
  touched, and a failure to delete never stops the plugin starting.
- Fix: Podcast Discovery always returned 404 when enabled. Podcast Index sends the envelope's
  `status` as a JSON boolean, but it was bound to a string, so the whole recent-feeds payload
  failed to deserialize. Both the boolean and the documented string form are now accepted, and
  an unusable payload is logged with the value exactly as it arrived.
- Added opt-in email sign-in. A client posts an email address, the server mails a single-use
  link, and confirming that link signs the waiting device in — no password, and no typing on a
  TV remote. The email can be opened on any device, so it works for tvOS; when it is opened on
  the signing-in device itself, the confirmation page also offers a deep link straight back into
  the app. Unrecognised addresses can optionally register, in which case the new account is
  created disabled and copies an administrator-chosen template user's permissions, so nothing is
  accessible until an administrator enables it. SMTP host, port, security, credentials and
  from-address are configured in the plugin settings, along with link lifetime and rate limits;
  a "send test email" button reports the mail server's own error when submission fails. The
  endpoint reports an explicit error rather than a silent success when SMTP is not configured.
- Fix: an audio filter matched files that had each thing you asked for, but never in
  the same track. Asking for AC-3 in 5.1 returned 444 movies on a test library, of which
  only 247 had an AC-3 track that was itself 5.1 — the rest were "DTS 5.1 main track plus
  AC-3 2.0 commentary" files that answered "has AC-3" and "has six channels" separately.
  Codec, channel count and spatial format are now read per audio track and have to hold on
  ONE of them. A filter naming a single audio facet is unaffected. The values offered by
  /Capabilities are unchanged.
- Music libraries can now be filtered by codec and channel count. Tracks were never
  catalogued, so every audio filter over a music library returned nothing at all while the
  same library unfiltered returned 11,022 tracks.
- Release-date recovery reads the FILE NAME first and falls back to date added, and
  understands two-digit-year release names (Name.25.02.05.Title). Date added is when a
  file reached the server, not when it was released: on a 650-item dry run, leading with
  it produced 18 distinct dates with 605 identical, while the name gave 98 spanning 2013
  to 2026.
- Release-date recovery is chosen PER LIBRARY. - Added opt-in release-date recovery. Downloaded YouTube content carries its upload
  date only in the file name, so Jellyfin stores no premiere date and reads the leading
  YYYYMMDD as a production year like 20250823 — those items then cannot appear in any
  view ordered by release date, on any client. A new scheduled task, "Recover missing
  release dates", reads the date from the production-year stamp, an sYYYY.eMMDDnn name,
  or a bare YYYYMMDD run, and writes it along with the corrected year. Off by default,
  previews to the log until an administrator turns preview off, and never modifies an
  item that already has a release date.
- Adds the seamless Marquee Companion panel to Jellyfin Web without manual web-client changes. - Adds paired Jellyfin 10/.NET 9 and Jellyfin 12/.NET 10 package builds. - Removes podcast discovery and email sign-in, including their settings, API endpoints,
  and bundled mail dependencies. Existing email mappings and Jellyfin accounts are untouched.
- Organizes settings into Library filtering, Release dates, Apple Watch, and Profile PINs.
  Release-date recovery now uses Off, Preview only, or Apply changes; the task still runs
  from Dashboard > Scheduled Tasks.

  rejection, and feeds dropped during validation — including a per-rule tally of what was
  dropped.
- Removes the YouTube trailer resolver. Clients now hand YouTube trailers to the YouTube
  app instead, so the server no longer downloads, verifies, updates, or executes yt-dlp or a
  JavaScript runtime.
- Removes the yt-dlp and JavaScript-runtime downloads earlier versions installed. Those
  binaries are unreachable now the resolver is gone, so the plugin reclaims the directory it
  created rather than leaving an administrator to find it. Only its own install root is
  touched, and a failure to delete never stops the plugin starting.
- Fix: Podcast Discovery always returned 404 when enabled. Podcast Index sends the envelope's
  `status` as a JSON boolean, but it was bound to a string, so the whole recent-feeds payload
  failed to deserialize. Both the boolean and the documented string form are now accepted, and
  an unusable payload is logged with the value exactly as it arrived.
- Added opt-in email sign-in. A client posts an email address, the server mails a single-use
  link, and confirming that link signs the waiting device in — no password, and no typing on a
  TV remote. The email can be opened on any device, so it works for tvOS; when it is opened on
  the signing-in device itself, the confirmation page also offers a deep link straight back into
  the app. Unrecognised addresses can optionally register, in which case the new account is
  created disabled and copies an administrator-chosen template user's permissions, so nothing is
  accessible until an administrator enables it. SMTP host, port, security, credentials and
  from-address are configured in the plugin settings, along with link lifetime and rate limits;
  a "send test email" button reports the mail server's own error when submission fails. The
  endpoint reports an explicit error rather than a silent success when SMTP is not configured.
- Fix: an audio filter matched files that had each thing you asked for, but never in
  the same track. Asking for AC-3 in 5.1 returned 444 movies on a test library, of which
  only 247 had an AC-3 track that was itself 5.1 — the rest were "DTS 5.1 main track plus
  AC-3 2.0 commentary" files that answered "has AC-3" and "has six channels" separately.
  Codec, channel count and spatial format are now read per audio track and have to hold on
  ONE of them. A filter naming a single audio facet is unaffected. The values offered by
  /Capabilities are unchanged.
- Music libraries can now be filtered by codec and channel count. Tracks were never
  catalogued, so every audio filter over a music library returned nothing at all while the
  same library unfiltered returned 11,022 tracks.
- Release-date recovery reads the FILE NAME first and falls back to date added, and
  understands two-digit-year release names (Name.25.02.05.Title). Date added is when a
  file reached the server, not when it was released: on a 650-item dry run, leading with
  it produced 18 distinct dates with 605 identical, while the name gave 98 spanning 2013
  to 2026.
- Release-date recovery is chosen PER LIBRARY. - Added opt-in release-date recovery. Downloaded YouTube content carries its upload
  date only in the file name, so Jellyfin stores no premiere date and reads the leading
  YYYYMMDD as a production year like 20250823 — those items then cannot appear in any
  view ordered by release date, on any client. A new scheduled task, "Recover missing
  release dates", reads the date from the production-year stamp, an sYYYY.eMMDDnn name,
  or a bare YYYYMMDD run, and writes it along with the corrected year. Off by default,
  previews to the log until an administrator turns preview off, and never modifies an
  item that already has a release date.

  plugin id, and behavior unchanged).

  values offered for a library are drawn only from items in that library, so any

  matches episodes and returns the shows that have at least one matching episode.

versions.changelog:
## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.16.

## Features
- Frames are no longer taken from inside media segments, so intros, credits, recaps, previews, and commercials stay out of generated artwork
- New Avoid Media Segments setting under Frame Extraction, with a checkbox for each kind of segment to avoid, all on by default
- Segments come from a media segment provider turned on for the library, so items without any extract as before

## Developer
- Changing which segments are avoided discards the idle frame pools, so the next refresh extracts under the new choice

## Features
- New Cleanup Backdrops scheduled task under Library that reduces every item on the server to a single backdrop, keeping the first and deleting the rest along with their files
- The task has no default schedule, so it only runs when started by hand or on a trigger you add

## Features
- Primary and thumb images can name a second and third design, adding their versions of the same frames to the Edit Images picker
- New Edit Images Cache setting for how long rendered choices stay available, default 30 minutes
- Edit Images reuses the choices it already rendered when switching image type or page, instead of rendering every image again

## Fixes
- The Edit Images cache is bounded by size at 256 MB and releases expired images on its own, instead of holding them until the next render
- Every design in one Edit Images render draws from the same frames, even while other items are extracting
- Posters pass over a logo Jellyfin only knows by web address and use the next logo that can be read

## Developer
- Settings saved before 12.0.2.0 are no longer brought forward, so update through 12.0.2.1 first when coming from an older version
- Code, pages, and docs say logo rather than series logo, since films draw their own

## Fixes
- The Profiles page loads again instead of failing on a backdrop setting that no longer exists
- Posters with a logo draw the logo selected for a film, season, or series instead of falling back to text

## Features
- Artwork Generator is Episode Poster Generator rebuilt, with the same settings and a much wider job
- The repository moved with the name; re-add it as jellyfin-plugin-artworkgenerator to keep getting updates
- Draws posters, thumbs, backdrops, and text logos, where before there were only episode posters
- Covers series, seasons, films, music videos, home videos, and anything else with a video
- Configuration is rebuilt in three parts, designs, logos, and profiles
- Profiles decide which items get which images and which design draws each one
- Every design renders portrait and landscape, so one design covers a tall poster and a wide thumb
- A design's two lines are now simply the title and the subtitle, whatever the item is
- Text position and alignment work on every design, not just the few that had them
- New Bloom design, pooling color from the frame behind the text
- New Grid canvas, tiling several extracted frames into one picture

## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.16.

## Features
- Replace a library song's audio with a different YouTube upload from the Download tab; it keeps the song's file, tags, cover and playlist places.
- Choosing an album already in the library on the Import tab takes that album's cover.
- Imports join existing artist and album folders whose names differ only in case, punctuation or year, and take that album's name and year.

## Features
- Republishes 12.2.3.0, whose download did not match its checksum and could not install.

## Features
- Import Spotify playlists exported with Exportify, one playlist as CSV or all of them as a ZIP.
- Spotify imports embed Spotify's album cover and fill in the genre from Apple Music.
- Playlist tracks with an ISRC are matched to their official YouTube upload by it first.
- Generate a cover with the wand button on the Import tab; choose its text, order and colors in Settings → Album Art.
- Composer credits are stored as separate composers.
- Live, remix, cover, acoustic and instrumental versions are never matched unless the song's title names that version.

## Features
- When Apple Music has no cover, the album cover from the official YouTube Music track is used.
- Re-pitched, sped-up, 8D and nightcore uploads are never matched.
- Artists YouTube Music credits in another alphabet (such as Cyrillic) are matched by album or exact length.
- Re-importing a playlist removes queued or failed songs your library now has.

## Features
- YouTube matches must contain the song title, so another song by the same artist with a similar length is never downloaded instead.
- Importing rescans only the imported songs' folders instead of the whole library.

## Features
- Look up each download on Apple Music to fill in its title, album, album artist, year, track number and genre (Settings, on by default).

versions.changelog: If the plugin stopped working with "The poster overlay state file ... could not be read", this release is for you. The state file is now written atomically, so a server that dies mid-write can no longer leave it empty - which is what happened on the reference server when the VM was killed during the nightly run. An image uploaded just before a crash is now recognised on the next run, and a cached original without a record is never overwritten. New task "Rebuild poster overlay state": run it with the dry run on first. It rebuilds a record only where drawing today's badges onto the cached original gives the cover on the item again, and lists everything else by name without touching it. Do not delete a damaged state file - the old error message advised that, and it was wrong.

Fixes a badge that could not be taken off again. When an item lost its last badge - a duplicate was deleted, or it never really had a twin - the plugin was supposed to put the untouched cover back, and never did: the restore asked for a lock its own caller was already holding, then failed silently. A run with 222 items to restore restored none of them and reported a missing cache that was present. If your library carries labels that no longer apply, the next nightly run clears them.

Fixes the audio badge appearing on films that have no second copy at all.

Peers were matched by any shared provider id, which swept in TmdbCollection - an id every film of a series carries. All fifteen Star Wars films therefore counted as copies of one another, their audio formats differed, and a badge appeared where the rule says there should be none. Only ids that name a title are used now: IMDb, TMDb, TVDB and the custom id an NFO can set.

Also fixes the badge never appearing in the previous version, where copies were grouped by Jellyfin's presentation key. That key groups the rows of a series, but for a film it falls back to the item's own id unless the files were merged as alternate versions by hand, so two ordinary copies never shared it.

The badge itself is unchanged: ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on, drawn only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it, describing the track in the language you set rather than the technically best one.

Adds an audio-format badge - ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on - drawn only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it. Off by default.

The restriction is the point. Measured on a library of 2,346 films: of 105 groups holding more than one copy of a film, 7 differ in nothing the existing badges could show except the audio format. Every other film has no second copy at all, so a format badge there describes a file nobody is comparing to anything.

Which track it describes is configurable, as a list of languages, best first - the first one any track carries wins. This matters more than it sounds: 437 films carry several languages in different formats, typically a German AC3 beside an English DTS, and taking the best track badges such a film "DTS", which is true about the file and about a track its owner never selects. Setting a language therefore draws fewer badges rather than more, which is the intent.

Spelling is forgiving because the server is asked rather than a table in the plugin: "de", "ger", "deu" and "German" all name one language, for every language Jellyfin knows. A file with a single track always reports that one, whatever the preference says.

Within the chosen language only the best track counts - a film with Atmos, a DTS-HD track and a stereo commentary is an Atmos film. The label carries as much as the job needs: where two copies are both plain DTS and differ only in the channel layout, the layout is added.

The setting for merging Dolby Vision and HDR is now spelled MergeDolbyVisionAndHDR in code. Stored configurations are unaffected - the file keeps the old spelling on purpose, so a value anybody switched off stays switched off.

The settings page now previews on a real item, drawn by the server through exactly the code a run uses. It used to imitate the badges in SVG on a mock poster - a second implementation of the drawing rules, which had already drifted from the real one: the centred positions had to be taught to both, and the imitation estimated text width where the renderer measures it, so no pill was ever quite the right width.

The page sends the settings as they stand, saved or not, so a change can be looked at before it is kept. Nothing is written while previewing - not the item, not the cached original, not the stored configuration.

The category is not free text. The official catalogue uses exactly eight values, and one outside that set parses cleanly and then belongs to no filter at all - the plugin would quietly drop out of every category view with no error anywhere. The build now refuses a value outside those eight before it starts, rather than shipping one and finding out later.

Jellyfin's episode list shows a still in a container of its own proportions and takes the difference off the left and right, so a badge near either edge is cut in half - and raising the margin does not help, because the crop is proportional rather than a fixed number of pixels.

Centred sidesteps that instead of fighting it: the crop may take as much as it likes off both sides and a badge in the middle stays whole, so only the vertical distance still has to fit. Changed: a folder that says two independent things now gets two edition badges. "REMASTERED.EXTENDED" used to draw EXT alone, because both rules matched and only the first was ever used.

Collecting every match would be wrong the other way round - it would turn "Extended Directors Cut" into three badges for one version. So each rule now declares what kind of statement it makes: which cut this is, how the picture is framed or coloured, how the copy was mastered. Within one kind the first match still wins, so a combination like EDC stays a single badge; across kinds the badges stand side by side, with the cut first because that is what tells two copies of a film apart.

Measured over 2380 real folders, six carry two edition tokens and no folder carries two of the same kind, so this is a small and predictable change.

Added: episodes are read from their file name, so two copies of one episode in the same resolution can finally be told apart. A movie keeps its release tags in its folder name, but a flattened season is one folder with every episode beside each other in it, so for episodes the file name is the only place they live. The episode title is subtracted first, exactly as a film title is - otherwise an ordinary title like "The Extended Family" would be read as an edition - and the remaining text must contain a known release tag or it is discarded whole. versions.changelog:
## ✨ New Features

- **Notify chosen users**: tick non-admin users on the new **Settings** tab to show them the badge too.
- **Counts only**: they see how many plugins changed, and can't dismiss or restart.

## 🎨 Improvements

- **Tabbed plugin page**: the page is split into **Updates** and **Settings** tabs.

## ✨ New Features

- **Notify chosen users**: tick non-admin users on the new **Settings** tab to show them the badge too.
- **Counts only**: they see how many plugins changed, and can't dismiss or restart.

## 🎨 Improvements

- **Tabbed plugin page**: the page is split into **Updates** and **Settings** tabs.

## ✨ New Features

- **Removals are tracked**: uninstalling a plugin now shows on the **Plugin Updates** page and badges your avatar, just like an install, until the restart that applies it.
- **History of applied changes**: a collapsible **Previously applied** section lists what earlier restarts made live, grouped by restart. It keeps the last 50 changes and can be cleared.
- **Built for Jellyfin 12.0 and 12.1**: each release is now published once per server version, so the catalog offers a build that targets your server exactly.

## 🐞 Bug Fixes

- **One card per plugin**: installing and then updating a plugin before a restart shows as a single change, and installing then removing one shows nothing at all.
- **Manual task runs are safe**: running the plugin's startup task by hand from Scheduled Tasks no longer clears changes that are still waiting for a restart.
- **Sturdier saved state**: a damaged state file is kept aside as `updates.json.unreadable` instead of being overwritten, and one bad entry no longer costs the rest.

## 🐞 Bug Fixes

- **Nothing runs for non-admins**: the script checks who you are first, instead of every user's browser polling once a minute for an admin-only answer.
- **Far fewer checks**: every five minutes instead of every minute, and paused while the tab is in the background.
- **Smaller checks**: each check now asks only for the number it needs, instead of downloading every plugin's full release notes and throwing them away.
- **Switching tabs is free**: returning to the Jellyfin tab no longer triggers a fresh check.
- **Lighter on the browser**: the plugin now only keeps an eye on the page while a notification is actually showing, rather than constantly, for everyone.

## 📋 Notes

- The badge can now take up to five minutes to appear after a plugin is updated, rather than up to one. Opening the user menu always shows the current count.

## ✨ New Features

- **Plugin icon**: the plugin now has its own icon in the catalog and in your plugin list, instead of a blank placeholder.

## 🐞 Bug Fixes

- **Readable changelogs**: a plugin's release notes on the **Plugin Updates** page now appear properly formatted. Bold text, headings and links show as intended, instead of displaying the raw formatting characters around them.

## 📋 Notes

- Nothing to reconfigure. Updating takes only the usual restart.
- Still Jellyfin 12 only. The avatar badge and profile-menu entry need the [JavaScript Injector](https://github.com/n00bcodr/Jellyfin-JavaScript-Injector) plugin; the dashboard page works without it.

## Plugin Update Notifier 1.0.0.0

First release, for Jellyfin 12.

Jellyfin installs plugin updates in place but only applies them on the next server restart, and nothing in the UI tells an administrator that a restart is pending. This plugin closes that gap: it watches plugin install and update events and surfaces a clear, dismissible reminder until the server is restarted.

### Features

- Avatar badge: a dot appears on the admin's profile avatar the moment a plugin change leaves a restart pending.
- Profile-menu entry: a "Plugin Updates" item in the user dropdown, shown only to administrators, with a count of what changed.
- Dashboard page: lists every changed plugin, its old and new version, the release changelog, and a link to each plugin's source.
- Shared dismiss: dismissing hides the reminder for every admin session, not just one browser; a later plugin change brings it back.
- Self-clearing: the reminder disappears on its own after the restart it was asking for.

### Requirements

- Jellyfin 12 (this release uses APIs not present in 10.x).
- The avatar badge and profile-menu entry additionally require the [JavaScript Injector](https://github.com/n00bcodr/Jellyfin-JavaScript-Injector) plugin (4.0.0.0 or newer). The dashboard page works without it.

# 🎬 Media Bar Arrives on Jellyfin 12

Media Bar **3.0.0.0** brings support for **Jellyfin 12**, including compatibility with both the classic desktop experience and Jellyfin's newer modern web layout.

> ## 🙌 Huge thanks to MakD and the upstream contributors
>
> Media Bar itself is the work of **MakD and the contributors to the upstream Media Bar project**. The plugin I maintain is primarily a Jellyfin wrapper around that work, exposing configuration and integration points so it can be installed and managed cleanly as a Jellyfin plugin.
>
> A huge amount of effort has gone into keeping Media Bar working across Jellyfin's changing web interface, especially for Jellyfin 12. The features, UI work and frontend improvements in this release are built on that upstream work, and the credit for that belongs to **MakD and everyone contributing there**.
>
> My part is largely packaging, integrating and exposing that work through Jellyfin's plugin system.

## ✨ New Features

* Added support for **Jellyfin 12**.
* Added support for Jellyfin 12's **modern React/MUI home screen layout**, alongside the existing classic desktop layout.
* Updated the bundled Media Bar frontend to the latest Jellyfin 12-compatible upstream version.
* Added Jellyfin 12-specific styling so Media Bar integrates correctly with the new web-client shell while retaining the existing appearance on the classic layout.
* Media Bar continues to ship its frontend assets directly with the plugin, ensuring the version displayed in Jellyfin matches the plugin version you've installed.

## 🛠️ Improvements

* Synced Media Bar with the latest Jellyfin 12-compatible upstream work.
* Improved Media Bar placement within the Jellyfin 12 home screen across both supported layouts.
* Improved layout behaviour on taller displays, ensuring Jellyfin's home-screen rows remain below the Media Bar content rather than overlapping its controls.
* Improved localisation handling when loading Jellyfin's translation chunks.
* Retained support for the **Get updates early** option for users who explicitly want to track unreleased upstream Media Bar changes.

## 🪲 Bug Fixes

* Fixed Media Bar being inserted in the wrong position when using Jellyfin 12's modern layout (#181).
* Fixed translated Media Bar strings falling back to English or producing JSON decoding errors for some languages (#185).
* Fixed home-screen rows overlapping Media Bar buttons on taller viewports.
* Fixed Jellyfin 12 layout differences that could cause Media Bar to render incorrectly compared with Jellyfin 10.11.

## ⚠️ Compatibility

* **Media Bar 3.0.0.0 supports Jellyfin 10.11.11 and Jellyfin 12.**
* Users on older Jellyfin 10.x versions should remain on a compatible **2.x** Media Bar release.
* Jellyfin 12 support includes both the **classic Desktop layout** and the newer **modern React/MUI layout**.
* A compatible **File Transformation 3.x** release is required.
* If you're using the **Get updates early** option, unreleased upstream Media Bar changes may behave differently from the frontend bundled and tested with this plugin release.

## Contributors

* austinnorgaard
* judarange

## ❤️ Support

If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27).

Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

versions.changelog:
Same plugin as v12.0.1.0 - no functional changes. It exists so that servers
upgraded from Jellyfin 10.11 to Jellyfin 12 automatically pick up the correct
build.

Bug Fixes:
- Upgrading Jellyfin from 10.11 to 12 left the plugin showing "Not supported".
  Each release published its 10.11 and its 12 build under the same version
  number, so a server that had installed the 10.11 build kept it after the
  upgrade - Jellyfin saw no newer version to offer, and the 10.11 build cannot
  run on Jellyfin 12. This release is published for Jellyfin 12 only, so those
  servers now see an update and repair themselves. Jellyfin 10.11 servers are
  unaffected and stay on v12.0.1.0.

Full changelog: https://jellyfin-smartlists-plugin.dinsten.se/changelog/stable/

The first stable release for Jellyfin 12, and the biggest update yet - 22 release
candidates of work since v10.11.30.2. Jellyfin 10.11 is still fully supported.

Jellyfin 12:
- Full support for Jellyfin 12, including the final 12.0.0 release
- Jellyfin 10.11 continues to receive the same updates

New features:
- List templates: one-click starting points on the Create tab
- Hide when empty: a list disappears while nothing matches, and returns on its own
- Group results into collections: turn an item search into a collection of collections
- Collection and Playlist media types: build collections of collections or playlists
- Smart collections now carry genres, studios, parental rating and total runtime
- Smart list badge on generated covers, with a setting to turn it off
- Integration API so other tools can create and manage smart lists
- Bumpers, and random group selection
- New rule field: User Rating
- Date rules can include items whose date is missing from metadata
- New settings for default media types and for hiding new lists when empty

External lists:
- New providers: ListenBrainz and Scrob
- Music lists match tracks via MusicBrainz, one library item per matched track
- User-Agent setting for when a provider starts blocking requests

Sorting:
- Least Recently Watched Round Robin, and Shuffled Round Robin
- Round Robin can group by Collection and order items within each group
- Crossover episodes that aired close together play back-to-back, with an Air Window setting
- Play Count (all users) and Last Played (all users)

Improvements:
- Large speed-up for expensive rules - people, languages, resolution and more are read once per refresh
- Parent tags, studios and genres are found at every level above an item, including the library
- Only fully watched episodes advance the Least Recently Watched rotation
- Weekly cleanup removes leftover playlists and collections whose list is gone
- Rule groups are named consistently throughout; the sort option is now Rule Group Order

Bug fixes:
- Titles containing numbers sort correctly - "Season 2" before "Season 10"
- The Resolution sort did nothing and left lists sorted by name
- Episodes came back unordered when Season/Episode was combined with another sort
- A series showed a play count of 0 even when every episode was watched
- Items with no release date no longer match "before", "older than" and "not equals"
- IMDb lists, charts and awards failed to load with a "Forbidden" error
- Configuration pages loaded blank behind a reverse proxy, or with Cloudflare Rocket Loader
- Smart collections disappeared when the TMDbBoxSets plugin was installed
- Duplicates left behind by a failed deletion are detected and cleaned up
- List names can contain : * ? < > | " / and \ again
- Saving a list now reports why it failed instead of appearing to do nothing
- A failed save no longer discards what you typed
- Deleting a list right after editing it no longer brings it back

Existing lists may change:
- Rules checking parent values now look at every level above an item, so they match more
- Music lists are the most visible case: artist folder and library values now count
- Similar To applies within its own rule group instead of filtering the whole list
- Smart collections now carry aggregated genres/studios/runtime, so other lists may match them
- Include-only checkboxes are migrated automatically to Name rules

Full changelog: https://jellyfin-smartlists-plugin.dinsten.se/changelog/stable/

versions.changelog:
## v1.7.0.0
### New
- Jellyfin 12 support. Every release now ships two builds, one for Jellyfin 12 and one for Jellyfin 10.11, and Jellyfin installs the right one for your server automatically.
- Jellyfin 10.11.0 and newer are supported again. The previous release required at least 10.11.6.
- New "Disable rate limiting" option for self-hosted LRCLIB servers. It removes the delay between requests, which speeds up large libraries. Requests to the public lrclib.net stay rate limited.
### Fixes
- Tracks that only have an album artist tag (compilations, classical music, many rips) now get lyrics. Strict search used to give up without an artist tag, and fuzzy search ignored the album artist entirely.
- Fuzzy search now tries every artist tagged on a track instead of only the first one.
- A system clock jump (NTP correction, VM resume) can no longer stall lyric requests.

## v1.7.0.0
### New
- Jellyfin 12 support. Every release now ships two builds, one for Jellyfin 12 and one for Jellyfin 10.11, and Jellyfin installs the right one for your server automatically.
- Jellyfin 10.11.0 and newer are supported again. The previous release required at least 10.11.6.
- New "Disable rate limiting" option for self-hosted LRCLIB servers. It removes the delay between requests, which speeds up large libraries. Requests to the public lrclib.net stay rate limited.
### Fixes
- Tracks that only have an album artist tag (compilations, classical music, many rips) now get lyrics. Strict search used to give up without an artist tag, and fuzzy search ignored the album artist entirely.
- Fuzzy search now tries every artist tagged on a track instead of only the first one.
- A system clock jump (NTP correction, VM resume) can no longer stall lyric requests.

versions.changelog:
✨ New Features

* Added Studio / Network, Decade, Hidden Gems and Finish These Collections sections, and enabled the previously developed Starring and Directed By sections (PR #292, @n00bcodr).
* Added per-section previews to the admin configuration page, allowing section results to be previewed before saving (PR #288, @n00bcodr).
* Added a new Add/Remove section workflow to make managing enabled sections easier (PR #288, @n00bcodr).

🛠️ Improvements

* Reworked section ordering in the admin configuration page with drag-and-drop support, including support for moving groups of sections that share the same order (PR #288, @n00bcodr).
* Added section information popovers using the new admin descriptions (PR #288, @n00bcodr).
* Improved section naming fallbacks and fixed missing Genre section localisation in the admin interface (PR #288, @n00bcodr).
* Escaped section metadata when rendering the home screen and settings interface so titles and names containing markup are displayed safely as text (PR #304, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv).

🪲 Bug Fixes

* Fixed #297 where users on Jellyfin 12 could receive items from libraries they did not have access to in Latest Movies, Latest Shows, Recently Added and Genre sections (PR #301, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv).
* Fixed #298 where authenticated users could access another user’s Home Screen Sections data by supplying that user’s ID. User-scoped endpoints are now bound to the authenticated user (PR #302, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv).
* Fixed #298 by restricting section registration to administrators and limiting registered section result endpoints to the originating server (PR #303, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv).

🌐 Translations

* Completed missing Spanish and Catalan translations (PR #293, @GospelBG).
* Added Greek translations (PR #299, @KaliDarkzy).

⚠️ Compatibility

* Added support for Jellyfin 12.2.
* Jellyfin 10.11.11 remains supported.

Contributors
